objective: Computation and proof. Describe every new knot at a single opened cut: its size, whether it meets the removed line's hub, and which port patterns its near and far parts allow. Test whether new knots arise only when the hub and one near point pin a complementary pair of port patterns that one far point separates, and say what decides creation then. Prove the local reduction: a derivation of a three-point knot stays inside its four-point extensions.
status: Proved by HANDLE-EMERGENCE-20261102-001B-P001: every new knot at a single opened cut (936 over the census pairs) has three points, one in the removed line's hub, one near point off the ports, one far point; the hub and near point pin all three ports to one pattern and the far point separates it, which no single port carries (join lemma; locality of three-point generation by the size lemma); pin-and-separate is necessary, not sufficient; in the Fano every removed line meets the closing line, the hub is tied to that port and the pinned odd port is that port
